reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the formation of a single-phase (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2 and its superior oxidation resistance relative to most individual diborides, but it provides no data on lower-temperature densification (~1700 °C) or liquid-metal corrosion resistance, leaving two key premises unsupported.
premises: Equiatomic Hf, Ta, Nb, Ti additions to ZrB2 can form a single-phase high-entropy diboride
The high-entropy diboride can be densified at ~1700 °C via SPS
The high-entropy diboride exhibits improved oxidation resistance compared to single-phase ZrB2 and its individual components
The high-entropy diboride exhibits improved resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion
